newsitem.title: USA: Most U.S. debt futures rise near outset.
newsitem.headline: Most U.S. debt futures rise near outset.

text.p: Most U.S. interest rate futures rose modestly near the outset, with September Treasury bond futures extending their recent run higher.

September T-bond futures rose to a high early in pit trading at 116-09/32, that contract's highest level since early February 1996. On a daily continuation chart, lead-month T-bond futures hit a high of 116-12/32 on December 4, 1996.

Traders tied the continued ebullience to technicals as well as fundamentals showing economic growth with scant inflation pressure plus expectations that upcoming supplies will not undermine the market's firmness.

Treasury will announce the size of its early-August quarterly refunding Wednesday afternoon. Consensus estimates peg the total size of the refunding package at $40.0 billion, comprised of $16.0 billion in three-year notes, $14.0 billion in 10-year notes and $10.0 billion in 30-year bonds.
Ideas that future supplies might not balloon added lift as the market eyed the federal balanced budget package that could help keep down government borrowing needs.
"The market's in great shape," said a T-bond futures floor broker. "We're ultimately going to six percent (yield)." Such a drop in yield would place lead-month futures near 121-16/32.

"I think that's absolutely in the back of everyone's minds," added another floor broker of the potential effect on supplies of balanced budget legislation that some expected have an effect by year's end.
He said that perception could foster demand at the August refunding as well. "Everyone's going to want them, especially the 30 years," he added.

Brokers reported good cash demand overnight, including talk of central bank buying of intermediates and more signs of mortgage-related buying of long bonds to hedge against rising mortgage prepayment risks as yields drop.
"There's no question that everybody's getting in their re-fi (mortgage refinancing) applications," he said.
The first broker also said a big seller of Treasury put options overnight added support.
Technically, the ability of September T-bond futures to hold above the 115-31/32 area encouraged buyers.
"This thing holding the 116 handle is pretty impressive," said the second broker, who put intraday support at 115-23/32.

At 0822 CDT/1322 GMT, Sept T-bonds rose 8/32 to 116-06/32, T-notes up 5/32 at 110-21/32, munis rose 6/32 to 121-24/32, Sept bills up 0.010 at 94.925, Dec Euros up 0.015 at 94.170. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750)) E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
